procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST FOR CONSULTING SERVICES 

SELECTION OF AN INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (IT) CONSULTANT   

FOR SRI LANKA DEPOSIT INSURANCE SCHEME

 

Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka

Financial Sector Safety Net Strengthening Project

Credit No. 7418-Lk

Assignment Title:  IT Consultant for Sri Lanka Deposit Insurance Scheme  

Reference No. : RE - LK-CBSL-531361-CS-INDV

 

1. Background

The World Bank (WB) is providing investment project financing to Sri Lanka under the Financial Sector Safety Net Strengthening Project (FSSNP - the Project). The objective of the project is to strengthen the financial and institutional capacity of Sri Lanka's financial sector safety net, with the focus on the Sri Lanka Deposit Insurance Scheme (SLDIS) leading to improvements in the financial and institutional capacity of SLDIS, as evidenced by improvements in its funding ratio, timely reimbursement of insured deposits in case of bank failures and enhanced public awareness about SLDIS. The project will be implemented by the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL), with the work led by the Deposit Insurance and Resolution Department (DIRD) of CBSL, which is responsible for the management of SLDIS.

CBSL is seeking a qualified consultant to conduct information technology (IT) needs assessment for activities of SLDIS, provide recommendations on areas to be improved in respect of IT requirements and facilitate such improvements.

 

2. Scope of the Assignment

Interested candidates are requested to refer to the attached Terms of Reference (TOR) for this assignment, which can be downloaded via the following link:
 

https://www.cbsl.gov.lk/sites/default/files/cbslweb_documents/about/tor_20260122_individual_consultant_selection_method_under_the_financial_sector_safety_net_strengthening_project_financed_by_the_world_bank_e.pdf

The scope of work is detailed in Section 4 of the TOR.

The proposed contract is a deliverable based assignment with DIRD, CBSL, where the consultant should dedicate his/her time and make focused effort to the successful completion of the deliverable within the specified timeframe.  The services of the Consultant   for SLDIS are required for approximate period of 07 (seven) months. The expected start date of the assignment is during the 1st quarter of 2026.

3. Qualification and Experience Requirements

The qualifications and experience requirements are outlined in Section 09 of the TOR. Accordingly, the following three criteria (items i to iii) will be used to determine the eligibility of candidates and evaluate the EOIs.

(i) Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or any other related field.

(ii) Minimum five (05) years of working experience in Business Process Analysis and/or other related Business Process Re-engineering (BPR) and ICT Management area.

(iii) Experience in working on the implementation of at least one (01) consultancy project in designing IT systems and IT solutions in finance, banking or other areas relevant to this assignment.

The remaining qualifications and experiences requirements (items iv to viii) that have been given in the TOR will be assessed during the interview process.

4. Selection Method

The individual consultant will be selected based on the qualification and experience, in accordance with the procedures set out in the 'The World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers- Procurement in Investment Project Financing- Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, November 2020’ and as per the Financing Agreement of the project and in accordance with the Individual Consultant method set out in the above World Bank’ procedures.

The attention of interested candidates is drawn to Section III, paragraph, 3.17 of the above procurement procedure/regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment as mentioned in the section 3.17 of the said regulations:

3.17 Consultants shall not be hired for any assignment that would be in conflict with their prior or current obligations to other clients, or that may place them in a position of being unable to carry out the assignment in the best interests of the Borrower. Without limitation on the generality of the foregoing, Consultants shall not be hired under the circumstances set forth below:

a. …..

b. …..

c. …..

d. Consultants (including their experts and other personnel, and sub-consultants), that have a close business or family relationship with a professional staff of the Borrower, or of the project implementing agency, or of a recipient of a part of the Bank’s financing, or any other party representing or acting on behalf of the Borrower, that is directly or indirectly involved in any part of:

i. the preparation of the TOR for the assignment.

ii. the selection process for the contract; or

iii. the supervision of the contract, may not be awarded a contract, unless the conflict stemming from this relationship has been resolved in a manner acceptable to the Bank throughout the selection process and the execution of the contract.

 

5. Submission of Request for Expressions of Interest

CBSL invites qualified individual candidates to express their interest in the IT Consultant position for SLDIS. Interested candidates should submit their Expressions of Interest (EOIs) along with supporting documents that demonstrate their qualifications and experiences.

Candidates are strongly advised to include certified copies of the required documents and a completed checklist provided in Annex I. EOIs submitted without the certified copies will not be considered for evaluation.

EOIs must be submitted in writing to the address below (in person, by mail, or via email) by no later than 1400 hrs. in Sri Lanka time on 23 February 2026.  

EOIs sent via email must be submitted as password-protected PDF files, with the subject line " IT CONSULTANT FOR SLDIS", no later than 1400 hrs. in Sri Lanka time on  23  February 2026  The passwords for the PDF files must be sent separately by 1415 hrs. in Sri Lanka time on the same day.

Le Ministère de l’Economie, du Plan et de la Coopération Internationale a reçu un financement de la Banque Mondiale pour financer le Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (HISWACA- SOP2), et à l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit pour effectuer des paiements au titre des Marchés d’Acquisition des équipements de formation et de sensibilisation dans le cadre des activités du quatrième Recensement Général de la Population et de l’Habitation(RGPH-4)  dont l’Institut Centrafricain des Statistiques et des Etudes (ICASEES) est l’organe d’exécution.

 

La Coordination Nationale du Projet sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour l’Acquisition des équipements de formation et de sensibilisation, dans le cadre des activités du quatrième Recensement Général de la Population et de l’Habitation(RGPH-4). La procédure sera conduite par mise en concurrence nationale en recourant à un Appel d’Offres (AO) telle que définie dans le « Règlement applicable aux Emprunteurs – Passation des Marchés dans le cadre de Financement de Projets d’Investissement au point 5.4 (procédures nationales de passation des marchés) de la Banque Mondiale (« le Règlement de passation des marchés » - édition courante), et ouverte à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans les Règles de passation des marchés.

  1. Les Soumissionnaires intéressés et éligibles peuvent obtenir des informations auprès de la Direction Générale de l’ICASEES/Coordination du Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (HISWACA- SOP2), représentée par Monsieur Blaise Bienvenu ALI. email : blaisebienvenua@gmail.com et prendre connaissance des documents d’Appel d’offres à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous :

Institut Centrafricain des Statistiques et des Etudes Economiques et Sociales/Coordination du Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (HISWACA- SOP2, Avenue Gamal Abdel NASSER B.P.696 Bangui République Centrafricaine à côté de l’hôtel JM Résidence, en face de la villa Nasser. Site web : www.icasees.org.

 

  1. Le Dossier d’Appel d’offres en Français peut être acheté par tout Soumissionnaire intéressé en formulant une demande écrite à l’adresse ci-dessous contre un paiement non remboursable de cinquante mille (50 000) Francs CFA en espèce.
  2. Les offres devront être remises à l’adresse ci-dessous au plus tard  le lundi 14 juillet 2025 à 11 heures 00 minute. La soumission des offres par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Les offres remises en retard ne seront pas acceptées. Les offres seront ouvertes en présence des représentants des soumissionnaires et des personnes présentes à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous le lundi 14 juillet 2025 à 11heures 00 minute. 
  3. Les offres doivent être accompagnées d’une garantie Bancaire pour un montant de : Dix millions deux cent vingt- deux mille (10.222.000) FCFA.

GOVERNMENT OF SOMALILAND

Request for Expressions of Interest (REOI)

 Country:            Government of Somaliland

project name:  Somali Enhancing Public Resource Management Project

Project ID:                  P177298                           IDA-E1360

Assignment Title: Consultancy Service for Budget Preparation Improvement (From Line-item Budgeting to Program Based Budgeting), credibility and Transparency Consultancy

Reference No:    SO-MOF-SL-527067-CS-CQS

Place of assignment: Hargeisa, Somaliland

 The Government of Somaliland has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Enhancing Public Resource Management Project (SERP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The Consulting Services (the Services) include five key areas: 1) designing a Program-Based Budgeting (PBB) framework. 2) establishing program classification systems and a Medium-Term Fiscal Framework (MTFF). 3) strengthening the budgeting, planning and controls of Somaliland government institutions which are counted in the national budget. 4) formulating a fiscal decentralization framework. 5) conducting capacity-building training and workshops. 6) promoting stakeholder engagement for budget transparency and recommendations for the 3-year PBB reform implementation.

The detailed Terms of Refence (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website:  https://slmof.org, or it can be provided upon submission of application in person or by e-mail. The e-mail address is provided below.

The Somaliland Ministry of Finance and Economic Development (MoF&ED) now invites the eligible consulting firm (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. (Brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff, etc.).  The short-listing criteria are as follows:

  1. Core business of the firm and At least 10 years in business (general experience in public sector budgeting, fiscal decentralization Planning, or financial management,) particularly with the implementation of PBB and intergovernmental transfers in developing countries.
  2. Experience of conducting similar assignments (At least 10 years of experience in implementing Program Based Budgeting (PBB) systems in developing countries, Extensive knowledge of public financial management (PFM) reforms, particularly PBB implementation in developing countries, experience in conducting institutional capacity assessments and designing training programs, proven track record in budget automation and digital PFM tools.
  3. Experience of relevant services in familiarity with Financial Management Information Systems (FMIS) upgrades and integrations, prior experience in providing technical assistance to governments in developing countries, Ability to design and implement performance monitoring frameworks and indicators, demonstrated success in stakeholder engagement and consensus building, particularly with government ministries and development partners, strong project management skills, including planning, execution, and reporting.
  4. Technical and managerial organization of the firm. (Provide the structure of the organization and CVs of staff). The Qualifications and Experience of Key Experts shall not be included in the shortlisting criteria]. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Financing - Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services dated July 2016 and revised in November 2017 August 2018, November 2020, September 2023 and March 2025, (Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualification but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub consultancy. In case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations.

Interested Consultant may obtain further information at the address below during office hours from 8:30 am to 3.30 pm Hargeisa time (Excluding public holidays).

procnotices.notice_text:
GOVERNMENT OF SOMALILAND

REQUEST FOR EXPERESSION OF INTEREST FOR IPSAS AND IFRS IMPLEMENTATION TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE

 A. Background

The Government of Somaliland has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Somali Enhancing Public Resource Management Project (SERP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services (individual consultant). The assignment involves a capacity-building initiative for Office of the Accountant General (OAG) to comply with and adopt IPSAS for the preparation of government financial statements for accounting periods. given the complexity of IPSAS implementation. it is essential to ensure the correct accounting treatment to minimize non-compliance risks and update organizational accounting and other relevant policies to reflect changes required by the new accounting standards.

B. Objective(s) of the Assignment

  1. To review and support the Office of the Accountant General in the implementation of the IPSAS Roadmap (2022–2027) and update the roadmap where necessary.
  2. To conduct a detailed diagnosis and identify gaps for adaptation of IPSAS cash basis II migration from IPSAS cash
  3. To provide capacity building to the Office of the Accountant General and all public entities to support the transition to accrual-based IPSAS, including a detailed gap analysis for migration from IPSAS cash basis II to IPSAS accrual basis.
  4. To review and enhance accounting and reporting documents, including policies, manuals, and regulations, to support full IPSAS adoption.
  5. To support completion of fixed asset registration and valuation for all public entities.
  6. To support the inclusion of all public entities’ GPFRs in the Government-Wide GPFR.
  7. Prepare training needs assessment to support the adaption of IPSAS and IFRS implementation.

C. Selection Criteria: The selection shall be based on qualification, experience and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience, and skills should be included:

D. Consultant’s Qualifications and Experience

      1. Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Public Finance, Public Administration, Business administration, or a related discipline.
  • Professional accounting qualification such as CPA, ACCA, or equivalent

     2. Experience:

  • Minimum of five (5) years of experience in public sector accounting or financial reporting.
  • At least three (3) years working with government institutions and donors, preferably in Somaliland or similar contexts.
  • Must have considerable experience in the field of IPSAS and IFRS
  • Familiarity with Somaliland PFM laws and regulations
  • Experience in capacity building and training delivery.
  • Prior experience with the international donors, Ministry of Finance, Accountant General’s Office, or Auditor General’s Office is an advantage.

E. Reporting and other Deliverables: The consultant will report to the Accountant General of the State and will provide monthly and quarterly reports to the SERP Project Coordinator.

F. Duration of Assignment: The assignment is expected to take 12 months.

G. The Ministry of Finance and Economic Development with the Office of the Accountant General invites potential candidates for technical assistance in implementing IPSAS as per the Terms of Reference. Interested Individual Consultants shall provide the following: (i) Curriculum Vitae (CV) with 3 reference persons; (ii) copies of certificates of academic qualifications; and (iii) cover letter indicating that they are qualified to perform the services.

H. Submission Requirements: The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14,3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non -Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, September 2023 and March 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

I. The Individual Consultant will be hired based on the World Bank’s Guidelines for Selection and Employment of Consultants (July 1, 2016, and updated November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, September 2023) and March 2025.

J. Mode of submission of Applications: Interested applicants can access additional information, including the detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment, by visiting the following website:   https://www.slmof.org or can be provided upon submission of application by e-mail or in person. The e-mail address is provided below from 8:30 to 16:00 pm Hargeisa time (Excluding public holidays).

K. Deadline: Expressions of interest (EOI) and CV must be delivered (by e-mail or in person) in a written form of hard copy (if not by e-mail) to the address below by 16th February 2026 at 4:00 pm (Hargeisa Time) – marked clearly as – IPSAS & IFRS TA.

Attention; Somaliland Enhancing Public Resource Management Project (SERP)

Ministry of Finance & Economic Development

Opp. of the Ministry of Education and Science

Hargeisa, Somaliland

                          REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

                 (CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT)

 

COUNTRY: São Tomé e Príncipe

Project Name: Regional Statistics Project - SADC

Loan Number/Credit Number: IDA-E1890

Description: Recruitment of a Consultant for the Analysis of data and Reports of the Household Budget Survey

Referência N.º 23/C/PER/2024

The Government of São Tomé and Príncipe (GoSTP) has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) Donation to cover the cost of the Regional Statistics Project - SADC and intends to apply part of this grant to consultancy services for the Recruitment of a Consultant for the Analysis of data and Reports of the Household Budget Survey to support the National Statistics Institute (INE).

The specific objectives of this consultancy are:

Under the authority of the President of the National Institute of Statistics (INE), the Poverty Analysis Specialist’s primary mission is to work in close collaboration with the Technical Implementation and Coordination Team (TICT) of the Household Budget Survey (HBS) at INE and with other specialists, ensuring the processing, analysis, and interpretation of data, as well as the production of technical reports and official poverty indicators

Therefore, the Agência Fiduciária de Administração de Projetos (AFAP) invites qualified consultants to formalize their applications, attaching a Letter of Intent addressed to the General Director of AFAP, Curriculum Vitae, Copy of ID, and proof of training, experience in similar work, etc.

The selection criteria are as follows:

  • A Master’s degree in Social or Human Sciences, or an equivalent qualification, particularly in the fields of Statistics, Economics, Sociology, Anthropology, Demography, or Mathematics, with specialization in poverty analysis;
  • At least five (5) years of professional experience in data processing and analysis, production of monetary and non-monetary poverty indicators, and preparation of Household Budget Survey reports;
  • Proven experience in drafting technical documents and strong analytical skills;

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers", February 2025 ("Procurement Regulations"), which sets out the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Interested consultants can obtain the Terms of Reference through the electronic address: sadc.procurement@afap.st and dg.procurement@afap.st.

Expressions of interest must be delivered to AFAP's premises, on the 3rd Floor, or sent to the email address sadc.procurement@afap.st and dg.procurement@afap.st until 4:00 p.m. (local time) on February 13, 2026, and must mention the reference and the name of the competition.

Agência Fiduciária de Administração de Projetos, January 30, 2026.

 

                                                                            The General Director,

 

                                                                            Hélio Silva Almeida
